recreation_prompt_markdown:
# Recreation Prompt

Create a mobile portrait browser game called **Pocket Prism Expedition**. It must preserve a simple creature-collection loop: the player taps Start Journey, holds a large central Prism Capsule for 1.5 seconds, receives one weighted-rarity creature, increments total encounters and that creature's saved count, views a reveal overlay, opens a Field Dex grid, filters by rarity, inspects discovered entries, and can reset only after confirmation. Do not add combat, movement, or new win/loss rules. Reinterpret the loop as a Pokemon-like creature-collector RPG fantasy using bright route-map scenery, elemental starter motifs, rival energy, readable portrait UI, rounded tactile controls, and a cheerful coming-of-age tone.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source truth
- genre: mobile-first creature collection / loot-box archive loop
- objective: hold the central object long enough to generate one weighted random creature, increase total encounters, and grow the unique collection toward 300 entries
- input model: tap/click CTA buttons; pointer/touch hold on central capsule for 1.5 seconds; early release cancels the encounter
- core loop: start journey, hold capsule, encounter creature, reveal result, tap overlay closed, inspect Field Dex, repeat
- fail/friction state: no traditional loss; reset confirmation can purge progress; early release prevents an encounter; rarity odds create collection friction

## Protected mechanics
- 1.5 second hold-to-complete timer and cancellation semantics
- weighted rarity roll, encounter count increment, per-creature inventory increment, localStorage persistence
- reveal overlay, archive grid, rarity filters, detail modal, reset confirmation
- scoped pointer handling so mobile UI buttons remain tappable

## Safe theming surfaces
HUD vocabulary, creature names/lore, focal capsule art, background, colors, fonts, reveal copy, archive labels, rarity styling, audio/GIF feedback, and mobile chrome are safe to transform because they do not alter collection logic.
